thread:
Julia (sales): Heads-up — Helion asked for a performance POC next week. Mixed workload: chat gen + embeddings + retrieval. They want sustained load + short bursts, multi-AZ failover, and private deployment with KMS. Can we draft runbook + cost estimate?
Sam (eng): Got it. Quick clarifying q: what's their steady-state and spike profile?
Julia (sales): Steady ~200 RPS (mostly embeddings), ~50 chat-gen RPS. Spikes up to ~1500 RPS for ~5–10m every 2 hours. SLO ask: p95 embedding <200ms, p99 gen tokens <400ms if possible.
Maria (eng-ml): For that mix we should use dedicated nodes, KV caching for chat, and 4-bit quant for embeddings model. Recommend prewarm for model shards.
Kevin (eng-sre): Ops note: multi-AZ means 2 active clusters or active/passive failover. Expect extra ~20–40ms cross-region; also need bandwidth headroom for burst.
Sam (eng): Runbook sketch: 1) baseline sustained run at 200 RPS for 30m; 2) 3x spike tests at 1500 RPS for 10m each with 10m cooldown; 3) failover drill switching region. Use vegeta for traffic shaping. Example command:
```bash
vegeta attack -rate=200 -duration=30m -targets=targets.txt | vegeta report -type=json > baseline.json
vegeta attack -rate=1500 -duration=10m -targets=spike_targets.txt | vegeta report -type=text
```
Sam (eng): targets.txt will hit embedding endpoints and chat endpoints in the ratio 4:1. Include warmup ramp of 60s.
perf-bot: Baseline run (200 RPS, 30m) finished: p50=85ms, p95=210ms, p99=342ms for embeddings; gen token throughput p95=370ms p99=610ms (underpowered gen nodes). Attached small CSV of metrics in thread (upload).
Maria (eng-ml): Notes from traces: gen tail dominated by model cold-start and KV-cache miss during large spikes. Preloading the KV cache and enabling prefix caching reduces p99 by ~30–40% in our tests.
Kevin (eng-sre): Security checklist: private deployment supports customer-managed KMS (AWS KMS / GCP CMEK). We log key usage to audit trail and can produce an HSM reference for enterprise. Also need to confirm TLS mutual auth for their on-prem connectors.
Julia (sales): Pricing question from Helion: what's ballpark cost for a 1-month POC (dedicated cluster + transient burst capacity)? Also asking about 3-month commit discount.
Sam (eng): Ballpark: POC (dedicated 8x A100-equivalent nodes + burst buffer) ~ $35k–$50k for 1 month depending on reserved vs on-demand GPU hours. 3-month commit we can offer ~15–25% discount depending on contract. Will confirm exact quote with pricing team.
Maria (eng-ml): Operational recommendation: enable caching + quantization profile for embeddings, pin a lighter gen model for burst fallback (reduce latency and cost). That helps keep p99 gen <500ms under spikes.
Julia (sales): Can we answer Helion's RSA/security questionnaire snippet for KMS + data residency? I can draft but need validation.
Kevin (eng-sre): Quick answer snippet: "Yes — Private deployment supports customer-managed keys (AWS KMS/GCP CMEK). All inference traffic is TLS 1.2+; disk encryption at rest with customer key; audit logs exported to customer-controlled SIEM via secure, push-only integration." Add SOC2 & penetration test cadence.
Sam (eng): Next steps: 1) schedule 2-hour run w/ Helion ops (we'll run baseline + 1 spike + failover); 2) I'll produce a short Results writeup template (SLOs, observed metrics, cost estimate, mitigation notes) after runs; 3) Pricing to confirm formal quote.
Julia (sales): Thanks — I'll propose Wed 10:00 PT to Helion. @Sam @Maria please confirm availability. :pray:
Sam (eng): I can do Wed 10:00 PT.
Maria (eng-ml): I'm good for Wed.
Kevin (eng-sre): I'll standby for failover window — may need to shift if maintenance collision.
Julia (sales): Perfect. I'll send calendar invite and attach Helion's security questionnaire.
Sam (eng): For the writeup, I'll include the vegeta commands, prometheus p95/p99 ranges, tail latency plots, and a short recommendations section. Minimal example JSON for results we output: 
```json
{
  "sustained": {"rps":200, "p95_ms":"210", "p99_ms":"342"},
  "spike": {"rps":1500, "p95_ms":"520", "p99_ms":"1200"},
  "notes":"KV prewarm reduces p99 by ~35%"
}
```
Julia (sales): Love it. Please keep the writeup tight — 1 page summary + appendix. I'll send the commercial ask after we get baseline numbers. :thumbsup:
